index.title: Background tasks
index.description: Monitor executions and retry failed or stuck jobs

retry_dialog.title: Retry {name}?
retry_dialog.description: A new execution is queued with the same arguments.
retry_dialog.retried_before_one: This one has already been retried once.
retry_dialog.retried_before_other: This one has already been retried {count} times.

retry_all_dialog.title: Retry all failed tasks?
retry_all_dialog.description: Every failed or stuck execution in the current view is queued again with its original arguments. Rows that already have a retry in flight are skipped.

worker_health.broker_unreachable_detail: Nothing can be queued or run until the broker is back. The counts below are the last state written to the database.
worker_health.no_workers_detail: The broker is up but nothing is consuming the queue, so this backlog will not move on its own.

tasks_empty.filtered_description: Executions exist outside the current search, status and queue filters.
tasks_empty.broker_unreachable_description: Nothing can be queued or executed until the broker is back. Tasks are not being lost — they are not being accepted.
tasks_empty.no_workers_description: The broker is up, but nothing is consuming the queue. Tasks enqueued now will wait rather than run.
tasks_empty.healthy_description: Registered tasks appear here the first time they execute.
tasks_empty.checking_description: Asking the broker whether anything is running to execute tasks.

workers.title: Workers
workers.description: Celery workers connected to the broker
workers.broker_unreachable_description: The connection to the broker failed, so nothing can be queued or run. Check this setting and confirm the broker is up.
workers.no_workers_description: The broker is reachable but nothing is consuming the queue. Start a worker locally with:
workers.routes_description: Which queue each task pattern is sent to, and which module set it.
workers.routes_empty: No task routes are configured, so every task goes to the default queue. Add routes in a module's task_config.py (TASK_ROUTES).

outbox.title: Outbox
outbox.description: Durable events waiting for delivery to their handlers
outbox.discard_confirm: Discard this event for {handler}? It will never be delivered.
outbox.empty_description: Every durable event has been delivered.
outbox.conflict: This event is being delivered right now, so it cannot be changed. The list has been refreshed.
outbox.gone: This event no longer exists. The list has been refreshed.

logs.title: Logs
logs.description: Retained application and task log lines
logs.empty_description: Nothing matches. Retained logging is off by default: turn on log_sink_enabled in the Background tasks settings, then restart the web process and workers.

settings_form.title: Background tasks
settings_form.description: How tasks are queued, run and tracked, and how long their records are kept.

execution_tracking.label: Execution tracking
execution_tracking.help: How much of each task run is recorded: everything, only final states, only failures, or nothing. Changing it needs a restart.

track_publish.label: Track publishing
track_publish.help: Record when a task is queued, not only when it runs.

outbox_mode.label: Event delivery mode
outbox_mode.help: Whether durable events are delivered by the task runner or inside the web process.

outbox_max_attempts.label: Maximum delivery attempts
outbox_max_attempts.help: Delivery attempts before a durable event is marked dead, from 1 to 100.

outbox_sweep_interval_seconds.label: Event sweep interval (seconds)
outbox_sweep_interval_seconds.help: How often pending events are looked up for delivery.

outbox_lease_seconds.label: Event claim lease (seconds)
outbox_lease_seconds.help: How long a claimed delivery may run before another worker can take it over.

outbox_handler_timeout_seconds.label: Event handler timeout (seconds)
outbox_handler_timeout_seconds.help: How long a handler may run per attempt. Leave empty for the longest value the lease allows.

log_sink_enabled.label: Keep logs in the database
log_sink_enabled.help: Store application and task log lines in the database. Needs a restart of the web app and workers.

log_sink_level.label: Lowest log level kept
log_sink_level.help: Log lines below this level are dropped. One of DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL.

log_retention_days.label: Log retention (days)
log_retention_days.help: How long retained log lines are kept, from 1 to 3650 days.

db_pool_size.label: Connection pool size
db_pool_size.help: Number of database connections each worker keeps open.

db_max_overflow.label: Extra connections allowed
db_max_overflow.help: Additional connections a worker may open when the pool is busy.

db_recycle.label: Connection recycle time (seconds)
db_recycle.help: Connections older than this many seconds are replaced when next used. 0 replaces a connection every time it is taken from the pool.

db_statement_timeout_ms.label: Statement timeout (ms)
db_statement_timeout_ms.help: Longest a worker database statement may run. Leave empty to use the app's own limit.

broker_url.label: Broker URL
broker_url.help: Address of the message broker that queues tasks, usually Redis. Changing it needs a restart.

result_backend.label: Result backend URL
result_backend.help: Address where task results are stored, usually Redis.

task_default_queue.label: Default queue
task_default_queue.help: Queue that tasks without a specific route go to.

task_routes_override.label: Task route overrides
task_routes_override.help: Send tasks to other queues without a code change. Enter JSON mapping a task name pattern to a queue.

visibility_timeout_seconds.label: Visibility timeout (seconds)
visibility_timeout_seconds.help: Tasks running longer than this are handed out again and may run twice. Leave empty for the default of one hour.

worker_max_tasks_per_child.label: Tasks per worker process
worker_max_tasks_per_child.help: Restart a worker process after it has run this many tasks. Leave empty for no limit.

worker_max_memory_per_child_kb.label: Memory limit per worker process (KB)
worker_max_memory_per_child_kb.help: Restart a worker process once it uses more memory than this. Leave empty for no limit.

task_reject_on_worker_lost.label: Requeue tasks when a worker is lost
task_reject_on_worker_lost.help: Put a task back in the queue if its worker dies mid-run. It may then run more than once.

task_soft_time_limit.label: Soft time limit (seconds)
task_soft_time_limit.help: After this time a task is asked to stop gracefully. Must be lower than the hard limit.

task_time_limit.label: Hard time limit (seconds)
task_time_limit.help: After this time a task is stopped forcibly. Must be higher than the soft limit.

worker_concurrency.label: Worker concurrency
worker_concurrency.help: How many tasks one worker runs at the same time. Leave empty for the default.

broadcast_invalidations.label: Share cache invalidations between processes
broadcast_invalidations.help: Lets every web and worker process hear when another one clears a cache. Without it, other processes keep stale data until their cache expires.

invalidation_channel.label: Invalidation channel
invalidation_channel.help: Name of the channel cache invalidations travel on. Leave empty to derive it from the database.

task_always_eager.label: Run tasks immediately
task_always_eager.help: Run tasks right away in the calling process instead of queueing them. Meant for testing.

task_eager_propagates.label: Raise errors from immediate tasks
task_eager_propagates.help: When tasks run immediately, let their errors surface to the caller.

stuck_after_seconds.label: Stuck after (seconds)
stuck_after_seconds.help: A running task with no heartbeat for this long is marked as stuck.

stuck_sweep_interval_seconds.label: Stuck check interval (seconds)
stuck_sweep_interval_seconds.help: How often running tasks are checked for being stuck.

purge_interval_seconds.label: Cleanup interval (seconds)
purge_interval_seconds.help: How often expired task records are deleted.

retention_days.label: Task record retention (days)
retention_days.help: How long finished task execution records are kept, from 1 to 3650 days.
